stem:
A student investigates the cooling of a liquid in a beaker.

The temperature *θ*ᵣ of the laboratory is measured using the thermometer.

Hot water is added to an insulated beaker, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The thermometer measures the temperature of the water. At time *t* the temperature of the water is *θ*.

A series of readings of *t* and *θ* are taken.

It is suggested that *θ* and *t* are related by the equation

*θ* = *θ*ᵣ + (*θ*₀ − *θ*ᵣ)$e^{-t/K}$

where *θ*₀ is the temperature at *t* = 0 and *K* is a constant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of ln (*θ* − *θ*ᵣ) on the *y*-axis against *t* on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *t* and *θ* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

The value of *θ*ᵣ is (18.5 ± 0.5) °C. Calculate and record values of (*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C and ln ((*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C) in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in (*θ* − *θ*ᵣ) and ln ((*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Plot a graph of ln ((*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C) against *t* / min. Include error bars for ln ((*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *K* and *θ*₀. Include appropriate unit.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the absolute uncertainty in your value of *θ*₀.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Determine the time *t* for the temperature to reach 25.0 °C.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A thermometer is held above water in an insulated beaker on a heat-proof mat, with a stand and bench shown.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table gives six time and temperature readings, with blank columns for temperature difference and its natural logarithm.
An unmarked graph grid has ln ((*θ* − *θ*ᵣ)/°C) on the vertical axis and *t* / min on the horizontal axis.
